public_rationale: Under the plain reading, AGI means an AI with broad human-level ability, including learning new tasks. No such system was recognised as of March 2026. ARC-AGI-3 launched on March 25, 2026 to test that kind of general learning. Humans scored 100% and frontier AI scored 0.51% (e1). Each lab's leading model scored under 1% (e2). Some industry figures said otherwise. Jensen Huang said 'I think we've achieved AGI' (e3). These were contested opinions, not a broadly accepted declaration. The claim that AGI 'still hasn't happened' holds on the ordinary reading.
limitations: AGI is undefined. A broad enough definition could change the result.
The benchmark results came out about two weeks after the post. They are used as evidence of the state of the art in March 2026.
The benchmark's scoring penalises inefficiency heavily, and some critics dispute the method.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of March 2026, AGI has not been achieved.

statement.excerpt: The board fired Altman, once AI’s golden boy, in November 2023 not because AGI had been achieved (that still hasn’t happened) but because he was “not consistently candid,” just like they said.
statement.document_title: BREAKING: Sam Altman’s greed and dishonesty are finally catching up to him

our_interpretation: Marcus gives no definition of AGI. Plain reading: no AI system had been widely and credibly recognised as artificial general intelligence (broad human-level ability across tasks, including learning new tasks) as of early March 2026.
A single executive saying AGI is here does not count as achievement. Independent tests of general ability that compare frontier systems with ordinary humans are the main measure.
Target period: March 2026. That is the month of the post and the month the normalized proposition names. Frontier models tested later in that month count as evidence of the state of the art then.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evaluations around March 2026 show frontier AI systems falling far short of ordinary humans on tests of general, novel-task ability, and no broadly accepted declaration of AGI exists.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A broadly accepted declaration or independent evaluation by March 2026 showing an AI system matching humans across general tasks, for example a recognised expert verification that AGI had been reached.

evidence.explanation: On a benchmark built to test general learning in unfamiliar settings, frontier AI scored far below ordinary humans in March 2026. That is inconsistent with AGI having been achieved.

evidence.excerpt: Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro led the pack at 0.37%. OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 came in at 0.26%. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 managed 0.25%, while xAI’s Grok-4.20 scored exactly zero. Humans, meanwhile, solved 100% of environments.
evidence.locator: paragraph after 'In brief', second paragraph of body
evidence.explanation: Each leading lab's frontier model of March 2026 scored under 1% on tasks humans fully solved. This supports the view that no general human-level system existed.

evidence.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang went on Lex Fridman's podcast last week and said, plainly, "I think we've achieved AGI."
evidence.explanation: A prominent industry figure claimed AGI had been achieved in March 2026. This is an opinion, not a broadly accepted declaration, but it shows the claim is contested.
